# Calcium Carbonate + Hydrochloric Acid

## Balanced Chemical Equation

$$\text{CaCO}_3(s) + 2\,\text{HCl}(aq) \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2(aq) + \text{CO}_2(g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$$

**Balance check:**

| Element | Reactants | Products |
|---|---|---|
| Ca | 1 | 1 |
| C | 1 | 1 |
| O | 3 | 2 + 1 = 3 |
| H | 2 | 2 |
| Cl | 2 | 2 |

## The Process

The reaction happens in two stages:

1. **Double displacement:** The H⁺ ions from the acid react with the carbonate ion, and Ca²⁺ pairs with Cl⁻. This briefly forms carbonic acid:
   $$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$$

2. **Decomposition:** Carbonic acid is unstable and quickly breaks down:
   $$\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2$$

**Net ionic equation** (Cl⁻ is a spectator ion):
$$\text{CaCO}_3(s) + 2\text{H}^+(aq) \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+}(aq) + \text{CO}_2(g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$$

## Type of Reaction

- **Acid–base (neutralization) reaction:** the carbonate acts as a base and neutralizes the acid.
- **Double displacement (metathesis)** followed by **decomposition** of H₂CO₃.
- It is often called a **gas-forming reaction**.

## Observable Evidence

- **Effervescence:** bubbling or fizzing as CO₂ gas is released. This is the most obvious sign.
- **Disappearance of the solid:** the CaCO₃ (chalk, marble, or limestone) dissolves as soluble CaCl₂ forms.
- **Slight temperature increase:** the reaction is mildly exothermic.
- **Mass loss:** in an open container, the total mass decreases as CO₂ escapes.
- **Rising pH:** the acid is consumed, so the solution becomes less acidic.
- **Limewater test:** bubbling the gas through limewater (Ca(OH)₂) turns it milky, which confirms the gas is CO₂:
  $$\text{CO}_2 + \text{Ca(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaCO}_3(s) + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
- **End point:** fizzing stops when either reactant runs out.

## Real-World Relevance

- Acid rain eroding marble statues and limestone buildings
- Antacids (CaCO₃) neutralizing stomach acid (HCl)
- Geologists identifying limestone with drops of dilute HCl ("fizz test")
